newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian managers lack aggressiveness, poll says.
newsitem.headline: Canadian managers lack aggressiveness, poll says.

text.p: Canadian executives are respected but not feared by international competitors, said a poll released by the Canadian arm of an internatinoal accounting and consultancy firm on Monday.

More than 90 percent of chief executive officers polled by Deloitte & Touche Consulting Group said Canadian managers are well regarded overseas, but less than a third agreed that Canadian companies were "very competitive" on the global stage.
A lack of aggressiveness was the most common shortfall cited by the 69 percent of respondents who said Canadians were "somewhat competitive."
"It's clear that many Canadian firms aspire to compete on the world stage," said Larry Scott, a senior partner with Deloitte Consulting.
"We believe that Canada has the capability to do even better - to turn those aspirations into reality. But to do so, we're going to have to become more aggressive," Scott said.
But the poll found that many executives -- 15 out of 52 surveyed -- were looking to expand internationally in the next year.
Eighty percent of respondents said expansion would involve exporting goods or services overseas, while 47 percent had decided to set up branch plants or sales offices.
The United States remained the preferred destination for Canadian expansion, with 22 percent of CEOs saying they would expand through the establishment of U.S. offices or plants, the poll said.
Mexico was a distant second at seven percent, while western Europe, China, Brazil and Argentina were each cited by five percent of managers as expansion targets.

The Deloitte Consulting survey canvassed the views of 52 Canadian CEOs, whose companies employ 350,000, generated C$90 billion (US$65.7 billion) in sales in 1996 and control C$110 billion (US$80.4 billion) in Canadian assets.
